what_this_is: The MoE thesis, measured. docs/MINING.md's first open surface was 'a model with less weight traffic per token', because the persist ceiling is 2*min(capacity, footprint)/step_traffic and the capacity is fixed by the device. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is the same architecture family, the same runtime, the same hook and the same box as the dense Qwen3.8-27B matrix in rtx5090-baseline-matrix.json - with a sparse MoE FFN reading 8 of 256 experts per token. Every number here is a control/candidate pair measured minutes apart on one RTX 5090.

model.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, unsloth UD-Q4_K_M GGUF, 22.1 GB
model._geometry_source: read from the GGUF's own metadata and tensor shapes, not from the runtime's defaults: block_count 40, full_attention_interval 4 (so 30 recurrent layers, confirmed by which blocks carry ssm_* tensors), ssm.state_size 128, ssm.group_count 16 (linear_q_heads), blk.0.attn_qkv.weight [2048, 8192] so linear_qkvdim 8192 and linear_v_heads (8192 - 2*16*128)/128 = 32, ssm.conv_kernel 4.
model._state_formulas: lin_state = linear_v_heads * linear_head_dim^2 * sizeof(float) (qwen35.cpp:560); lin_conv = (linear_conv_kernel-1) * linear_qkvdim * sizeof(bf16) (qwen35.cpp:559). Both formulas reproduce the pinned Qwen3.8-27B numbers exactly.

concurrency16.no_ceiling_because: the runtime did not batch this width, so the measured step time is one row at a time and a ceiling computed from it would describe a workload that did not run

concurrency32.no_ceiling_because: the runtime did not batch this width, so the measured step time is one row at a time and a ceiling computed from it would describe a workload that did not run

ceilings.coverage_note: the section 44 weights this ceiling covers. concurrency 16 and 32 are withheld because the runtime does not batch this checkpoint above 8 rows, so there is no concurrent decode at those widths to bound. A weighted figure over the remaining 0.60 would renormalise those weights away and read higher than the matrix can actually pay, which is the same mistake decide.py refuses for a partial result - so the per-arm ceilings below are the answer and the weighted one is not published for this model.

how_to_reproduce.build: integrations/sparkinfer/build.sh $WORK   # the same pinned commit; the hook is model-independent, it brackets whatever the runtime marks as a linear attention layer
how_to_reproduce.why_capture_node: production decode is a captured CUDA graph and a stream access-policy window is host-side state capture never records, so without it the persist family defers every window and applies no policy at all

the_concurrency_arms_are_not_concurrency.what: On this checkpoint the runtime stops batching above 8 rows. At 16 and 32 sequences it packed 127 of 2173 and 127 of 4205 tokens and decoded the rest one row at a time, which is why aggregate throughput at both is ~455 tok/s - BELOW the 503 tok/s single-sequence rate, and 5.4x below the 2456 tok/s it reaches at 8 rows.
the_concurrency_arms_are_not_concurrency.cause: launch_mmvq_q4k_rows refuses M > 8 (kernels/csrc/cuda/gemm/gemv.cu) and the bf16 launch_mmvq_rows dispatcher has no chunking loop, unlike its own _f32 sibling which chunks M into groups of 8. So the first Q4_K projection of a wider batch is refused, dflash_verify_short_run declines at layer 0, and decode_packed returns false for the whole batch. The runtime says so itself: '[dflash-verify] mmvq_rows refused type=12 N=16 n_out=8192 K=2048' followed by '[dflash-verify] declined at layer=0'.
the_concurrency_arms_are_not_concurrency.consequence_for_this_matrix: the concurrency-16 and concurrency-32 rows below are recorded because they were measured, not because they mean what their labels say. eval/real_eval.py now refuses such an arm by name.
the_concurrency_arms_are_not_concurrency.whose_bug: SparkInfer's, not RecurLocal's. It is the surface docs/MINING.md lists third, and it is worth two orders of magnitude more than anything this library does.

provenance.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, sm_120, 32 GB, 170 SMs, 1792 GB/s
provenance.note: One box for every arm. Graphics clocks cannot be pinned in this container, so only same-box interleaved deltas are trustworthy.
